messages:
alex: seeing a surge of DNS NXDOMAIN/timeout errors from edge pods in ap-southeast and eu-central, GPU node joins are failing and kube-provisioner is backing off.

maria: logs? cluster or egress?

alex: egress. pattern: a subset of NAT pools (10.240.32.0/27, 10.240.64.0/27) suddenly return SERVFAIL for our internal model-registry hostnames, then coredns in the edge k8s falls into retry/backpressure.

kevin: can you paste a few examples?

alex: ```
May 18 12:02:12 pod/loader-7d9f coredns[1]: lookup model-registry.internal.ap:53: SERVFAIL
May 18 12:02:13 kube-provisioner[9]: Failed to register node i-0abc123: dial tcp: lookup model-registry.internal.ap on 10.240.64.1:53: no such host
May 18 12:02:14 node-init[1]: kubelet backoff registering: timed out
```

samir: hmm sounds like negative caching + split egress behavior. Did we recently change TTL or enable EDNS?

maria: netops pushed an authoritative change an hour ago to shorten TTL for canary registry to 15s for fast rollouts. that might interact poorly with upstream caches.

jen: which resolver chain are edge pods using? systemd-resolved -> node-local-dns -> coredns? or straight to egress DNS?

alex: pods -> node-local-dns (hostPort 127.0.0.53) -> iptables NAT -> egress NAT pool -> provider DNS resolvers. node-local has caching enabled with negative caching of 30s.

kevin: and provider resolvers are returning SERVFAIL intermittently for the canary name? Could be EDNS size truncation or rate-limiting from upstream. netops, any throttles? @netops-bot

netops-bot: alert: recent authoritative server cluster reported sustained queries/sec spike; rate-limit policy applied to 10.240.64.0/27 and 10.240.32.0/27 between 11:58-12:10 UTC.

samir: there we go. rate-limited egress -> resolver returns SERVFAIL -> node-local negative cache stores NODATA/SERVFAIL -> pods observe failures even after upstream fixed until cache expires. backpressure on coredns due to retries.

jen: mitigation ideas? options: 1) flush node-local caches via daemonset restart, 2) add sticky egress so queries go via non-rate-limited NAT pools, 3) increase upstream rate limits, 4) bump TTL/disable negative caching temporarily.

alex: tried restarting node-local on a handful of nodes, those recovered. but still happening cluster-wide because NAT pool mapping is uneven.

maria: rolling restart as bandaid will be noisy, but doable. we should also pin DNS egress to healthy pools and avoid the two rate-limited pools. patching iptables egress-routes live? risky.

kevin: quick patch: add a DNS egress policy that prefers provider resolvers via 10.240.96.0/27 and marks the bad pools as lower priority. I can push a safe iproute change to the NAT allocation service to de-prioritize 64/27 and 32/27.

samir: do it. also reduce negative cache TTL on node-local to 1s for the canary domain using a per-domain rule if possible. that will reduce the impact window.

maria: opened a ticket with provider to lift rate-limits for our authoritative cluster.

netops-bot: task created: NAT-priority-update (link: https://tickets.internal/INC-2319) assigned to kevin.

kevin: rolling NAT-priority update starting in 2m, will re-route future queries away from rate-limited pools.

alex: once NAT re-route is live, i'll roll node-local daemonset restarts 50% at a time to clear negative caches.

jen: please monitor kube-provisioner backoff metrics and GPU node join rate. if joins don't recover in 10m we escalate to provider network ops.

samir: long term we should: 1) instrument per-egress DNS error rates, 2) expose negative-cache TTLs in console, 3) implement resolver affinity for control-plane service endpoints so node bootstraps use stable resolvers, 4) push upstream to honor EDNS and avoid truncation.

alex: agreed. immediate owners: kevin -> NAT-priority update, alex -> node-local restarts, maria -> provider ticket. tagging followups in INC-2319. :thumbsup:

kevin: done, NAT-priority patch applied to allocation service. new egress map excludes 10.240.64.0/27 and 10.240.32.0/27 for DNS flows.

alex: starting grad restart of node-local on 20 nodes. first batch good, DNS errors drop for those nodes.

maria: provider responded, lifted soft limits temporarily while they investigate.

jen: monitoring shows node join rate back to normal after ~6 minutes. closing the immediate incident but adding action items to the infra backlog.

alex: thanks all. summary for incident notes: rate-limited NAT pools caused upstream SERVFAIL -> negative caching in node-local -> kube-provisioner backoff -> GPU node join failures. mitigations: NAT-priority re-route, node-local cache restarts, provider rate-limit lift. followups logged in INC-2319.

sre-bot: incident INC-2319 transitioned to resolved (ops summary attached).
